Last September when Apple launched the iPhone 17, the countdown officially began for when the new flagship would break a 15-year-old record. That record requires more than a year to surpass, but based on current rumours, the iPhone 17 will take the crown first.

The iPhone 4 had an unusually long sales cycle

That record belongs to the iPhone 4, which went on sale in June 2010 and remained Apple's top iPhone until October 2011. Because Apple shifted its flagship release cycle from summer to autumn that year, the iPhone 4 sat on the throne for nearly 16 months.

For consumers planning to 'wait for the iPhone 5,' it was a particularly frustrating period. What Apple ultimately unveiled was the iPhone 4S, which looked nearly identical to the iPhone 4, with all the changes tucked inside: the debut of Siri, an upgraded camera, and improved performance.

The iPhone 4 also went through multiple release phases technically. AT&T was the exclusive carrier for the iPhone in the US and launched it first; six months later, Verizon joined as the second US iPhone carrier; and after a troubled 10-month wait, the long-awaited white model finally arrived.

Since then, no iPhone has managed to break the 15-month flagship sales record set by the iPhone 4. The closest was the iPhone 11 Pro, which stayed on the market for 13 months because the iPhone 12 was delayed due to the pandemic. Other exceptions exist, such as the gaps between the iPhone SE and SE 2, and then to the iPhone 16e, each stretching over four years, but these were intentional arrangements rather than flagship cycles.

iPhone 17 is set to break the record (but the situation is different)

The iPhone 18 is expected to arrive only in spring 2027, which means the iPhone 17 will sit at the top of Apple's main product line for roughly 18 months, surpassing the iPhone 4's record and setting a new benchmark for the longest standard iPhone sales cycle in history.

Model Launch Replaced by Duration at top iPhone 17 September 2025 iPhone 18, Spring 2027 (expected) ~550 days, ~18 months (projected) iPhone 4 iPhone 4S 477 days, ~15.7 months iPhone 11 Pro iPhone 12 Pro 399 days, ~13.1 months iPhone (2007) iPhone 3G 378 days, ~12.4 months

A key difference between the iPhone 4 era and today is that the Pro line did not yet exist. The long wait between the iPhone 4 and iPhone 4S was an upgrade drought for consumers hungry for fresh surprises.

From the most-liked comment posted by Rex Videos

I think it all comes down to how you define the word 'flagship'

During this cycle from iPhone 17 to iPhone 18, the Pro models will still be updated annually, and Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to launch alongside them.

The foldable iPhone will be the most significant hardware change in iPhone history, but the iPhone 17 is still poised to claim the record for the longest gap between standard flagship models.

The shortest iPhone cycle

As an aside, the shortest gap between iPhone upgrades may come as a surprise. The iPhone 12 to iPhone 13 cycle comes to mind, lasting only 11 months because Apple adjusted its release schedule after the pandemic-related delay.

However, although the iPhone X was announced in September 2017, it did not actually go on sale until November 2017, and the iPhone XS replaced it just 10 months later.
